content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, assignment).**

- **Section 20(d)** (p0142) prohibits assignment by either party without the other's written consent — no reasonableness standard, no affiliate carve-out, no successor/M&A carve-out.
- **Section 3(c)** (p0033) is worse and one-sided: Sparkling may not assign the Agreement at all "except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing," i.e. in Garman's absolute discretion.

Together these amount to a blanket prohibition on customer assignment with no M&A carve-out — walk-away territory under the rule, and short of the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on notice, consent not unreasonably withheld). There is no change-of-control provision anywhere in the document, so Garman currently has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control; the redline locks that in expressly.

Redline (validated, preferred position): adds a reasonableness standard on consent, a carve-out letting Sparkling assign to affiliates or a successor by merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets on written notice, a bar on Garman assigning to a competitor of ours, and a confirmation that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and triggers no Garman termination, suspension or re-pricing right. Section 3(c) is conformed so the licence restrictions no longer cut across Section 20(d).
